jurisdiction.name: Peru
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Peru has a framework AI law (Law 31814 of 2023) and a binding, risk-based regulation under it (Supreme Decree 115-2025-PCM), led by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers' Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation, and adopted its first National AI Strategy 2026-2030 in May 2026. Law 32314 of 2025 makes the use of AI an aggravating circumstance and adds deepfake offences to the Criminal Code. The data protection law and its 2024 regulation set rules on automated decisions, and the banking supervisor (SBS) has model-risk rules with AI-specific requirements.
lead_institutions: Presidencia del Consejo de Ministros - Secretaría de Gobierno y Transformación Digital
Superintendencia de Banca, Seguros y AFP (SBS)
Autoridad Nacional de Protección de Datos Personales
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from the official texts in El Peruano and on government sites. The national legal database's search and Congress's bill tracker could not be used. The AI ethics guidelines required by the AI regulation, the national adoption of the ISO/IEC 42001 standard and pending AI bills are tracked as leads. As a country of over 20 million people with fewer than 10 records, Peru is marked for a longer catch-up pass.

instruments.current_status: Approved by Resolución Ministerial N.° 152-2026-PCM dated 29 April 2026 and published in El Peruano on 1 May 2026. The RM makes the ENIA applicable to public administration entities and state companies (private actors may use it as reference) and requires each entity to approve an AI Action Plan of at least three years. Peru's first adopted AI strategy: the 2021-2025 draft strategy was never formally approved (stated in ENIA section 1.3). Record title corrected from the gob.pe page title.
instruments.summary: Peru's first formally adopted national AI strategy, prepared by the PCM-SGTD under the AI Law Regulation, with the objective of developing and strengthening AI governance and management nationwide for inclusive, safe and ethical use. It is organised in four strategic axes (AI talent and capabilities; AI-based innovation and entrepreneurship; ethical and regulatory framework, including mandatory NTP-ISO/IEC 42001 and guidelines on algorithmic transparency and impact assessment; citizen participation and collaboration), with roles for AI governance, a roadmap, resource allocation and monitoring. The approving resolution binds public entities to align their plans with it and adopt institutional AI Action Plans.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy; sets public-sector AI governance roles and action plans.

instruments.current_status: Published in El Peruano on 9 September 2025. The decree enters into force 90 business days after publication (the 1st, 2nd, 4th and 5th final provisions apply from the day after publication); no calendar effective date is stated. Obligations phase in by entity type (public sector 1-3 years) and, for private developers/implementers, by sector (1 year for health, education, justice, security, economy and finance; up to 4 years for other uses). Earlier id held an explanatory gob.pe page ('Conoce el Reglamento...'); re-pointed to the decree itself. The draft was pre-published by RM 132-2024-PCM.
instruments.summary: Regulation of Law 31814 (36 articles, six titles) setting Peru's risk-based AI regime: it classifies uses as prohibited ('uso indebido') or high-risk (e.g. health, education, justice, finance, access to basic services, hiring), requires algorithmic transparency, human oversight, privacy by design, security measures and a high-risk impact assessment, and sets general obligations for public entities (institutional AI policy, mandatory NTP-ISO/IEC 42001:2025, AI in digital-government plans) and for private developers and implementers (records, internal policies, training). It establishes the PCM-SGTD governance framework, an AI controlled-testing sandbox, the gob.pe/iaperu channel, a duty on PCM to approve a National AI Strategy within one year, and a complaints route for people harmed by AI systems.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Core binding AI rules: risk classification, prohibitions, high-risk obligations, sandbox, mandatory ISO/IEC 42001 adoption.

instruments.current_status: Published in El Peruano on 5 July 2023 (approved by Congress 13 June 2023, promulgated 4 July 2023). In force; implemented by the Regulation approved by Decreto Supremo N.° 115-2025-PCM (9 September 2025). A bill to amend it with private-sector AI rules is pending in Congress (see leads).
instruments.summary: Peru's framework AI law: it declares AI promotion of national interest, sets principles for AI development and use (risk-based security standards, multi-stakeholder participation, internet governance, digital society, ethical development, privacy) and defines AI, AI-based systems, emerging technologies and algorithms. It designates the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, through the Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation, as the national technical-normative authority that directs, evaluates and supervises AI use, and requires it to report annually to Congress on the National Digital Transformation Policy and the National AI Strategy.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding AI law; designates the national AI authority (PCM-SGTD).

instruments.current_status: Published in El Peruano on 29 April 2025 (approved by Congress 22 April 2025, promulgated 28 April 2025). In force.
instruments.summary: Amends the Criminal Code (Legislative Decree 635) and the Computer Crimes Law (Law 30096) to make the use, or misuse, of artificial intelligence or analogous technologies a general aggravating circumstance (art. 46). It expressly covers AI-generated content and deepfakes in child sexual abuse material (art. 129-M) and defamation (art. 132), adds aggravated fraud through AI manipulation of a third party's voice, image or movement (art. 196-A), and extends intellectual-property offences and the computer-crimes aggravation to AI use.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Criminal-law provisions specific to AI and deepfakes.

instruments.current_status: Dated 3 July 2011 on the Congress norm page on gob.pe (the law text is dated 'Dado en ... 2 de julio de 2011'). In force; its current Regulation is DS 016-2024-JUS (in force 31 March 2025), which replaced DS 003-2013-JUS.
instruments.summary: Peru's general data protection law, guaranteeing the constitutional right to personal data protection and setting principles, legal bases, data-subject rights, cross-border transfer rules and sanctions, supervised by the National Authority for Personal Data Protection (Ministry of Justice and Human Rights). Article 23 gives data subjects a right to 'objective treatment': not to be subject to a decision with legal or significant effects based solely on processing intended to evaluate aspects of their personality or conduct, which governs automated decision-making by AI systems.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Data protection law governing AI training and automated decision-making (art. 23).

instruments.current_status: Published in El Peruano (special supplement) on 30 November 2024 per the MINJUSDH press release; in force 31 March 2025 per the ANPD (120 calendar days after publication, art.: Primera Disposición Complementaria Final). Repeals DS 003-2013-JUS. Text read from the gazette copy published by the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores.
instruments.summary: New Regulation of the Personal Data Protection Law (135 articles), repealing the 2013 regulation. Relevant to AI, it defines profiling as automated processing, requires information on the existence of automated decisions including profiling, and article 87 details the right not to be subject to decisions, automated or not, with legal or significant effects based solely on automated evaluation without human intervention, with a duty to inform the data subject; it also introduces impact assessments, data protection officers and breach notification.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Implements automated-decision and profiling safeguards applicable to AI systems.

instruments.current_status: Resolution dated 6 January 2023 (Lima); in force the day after publication in El Peruano with gradual implementation. Amended by Res. SBS 03421-2023 and implementation deadlines changed by Res. SBS 03884-2024 (not reviewed).
instruments.summary: Binding SBS regulation requiring supervised financial, insurance and pension firms to manage the risk of models used in credit, market, liquidity, operational and AML/CFT risk management (model inventory, categorisation, governance, development standards, independent validation and monitoring). For models built with artificial-intelligence techniques it requires at least interpretability testing, hyperparameter optimisation and cross-validation or similar techniques to avoid overfitting, and validation must assess hyperparameter choices and overfitting.

organizations.name: Presidency of the Council of Ministers
organizations.ai_governance_role: Presidencia del Consejo de Ministros (PCM). Through its Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation (SGTD), it is the national technical-normative AI authority under Law 31814 (art. 4): it directs, evaluates and supervises AI use, issued the AI Law Regulation (DS 115-2025-PCM, with the refrendo of other ministers) and approved the National AI Strategy 2026-2030 (RM 152-2026-PCM); it runs the AI sandbox and the gob.pe/iaperu channel.

organizations.name: Congress of the Republic of Peru
organizations.ai_governance_role: Unicameral legislature (Congreso de la República); enacted Law 31814 promoting AI, Law 32314 adding AI to the Criminal Code and Law 29733 on personal data protection; receives the AI authority's annual report (Law 31814 art. 5); AI bills pending.

organizations.name: Ministry of Justice and Human Rights
organizations.ai_governance_role: Ministerio de Justicia y Derechos Humanos (MINJUSDH); its General Directorate exercises the National Authority for Personal Data Protection (ANPD), which supervises Law 29733 and its Regulation (DS 016-2024-JUS), including the right not to be subject to automated decisions; the AI Regulation refers personal-data matters in AI to it.

organizations.name: Superintendency of Banking, Insurance and Private Pension Fund Administrators
organizations.ai_governance_role: Superintendencia de Banca, Seguros y AFP (SBS), financial supervisor; its Model Risk Management Regulation (Res. SBS 00053-2023) sets specific requirements for models built with AI techniques (interpretability, hyperparameter optimisation, cross-validation, overfitting checks).
